[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Architectural properties — PHI data classification, dead-letter queue presence, observability instrumentation, idempotency enforcement — cannot be verified by structural file checks alone. They require execution-time validation of the deployed service's behavior. Without executable architectural tests, these properties are verified only by human review, which is inconsistent and cannot scale to autonomous AI generation volumes.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

Architecture Fitness Functions are a category of executable test specifically designed to verify that architectural properties — not application logic — conform to the rules encoded in a Golden Path. They run as pipeline stage gates after build, produce structured results contributing to the compliance evidence record, and distinguish between properties that can only be observed at runtime and those verifiable earlier. They are authored alongside each Golden Path, not after.
page_texts.6:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

- Verifying architectural rule compliance for any Golden Path workload class
- Enforcing properties that require code execution or service invocation to verify (not purely structural file checks)
- Any CI/CD pipeline where Golden Path conformance must be verified beyond file structure
page_texts.7:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- Architectural properties verified objectively and consistently on every pipeline run, not just when a reviewer remembers to check
- Human review effort redirected from structural verification to semantic correctness — the questions only humans can answer
- Pipeline stage gates prevent architecturally non-conforming services from reaching deployment
page_texts.8:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#target-audience]

## Target Audience

This pattern is intended for:

- **Platform Engineer**: Authoring and maintaining fitness function suites for each Golden Path workload class in the CI/CD pipeline
- **Enterprise Architect**: Defining which architectural properties require executable verification and encoding those rules in the Verification Contract
- **CI/CD Engineer**: Integrating fitness function stage gates into pipeline definitions and maintaining execution infrastructure
page_texts.10:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

The [Enterprise Architecture Verification Strategy](../../../../strategy/white-papers/engineering/enterprise-architecture-verification-strategy.md) establishes fitness functions as Layer 2 of the four-layer verification architecture. They form the bridge between structural conformance checking (Layer 1, [PTN-INFRA-GOV-001](../../infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-001-architecture-conformance-gate-pattern.md)) and pre-deployment policy evaluation (Layer 3, [PTN-INFRA-GOV-002](../../infrastructure/governance/PTN-INFRA-GOV-002-policy-as-code-enforcement-pattern.md)). Fitness functions verify the architectural decisions that can only be validated when code runs — they occupy the category of checks that are too semantic for file structure tests but too structural for application integration tests.
page_texts.11:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

Fitness functions run in the CI/CD pipeline against a locally started or test-environment-deployed instance of the service. They are implemented as test code (Go test, pytest, JUnit, or a shell harness) that invokes the service or inspects its compiled artifacts and asserts architectural properties. They are distinct from unit tests (which verify application logic) and integration tests (which verify inter-service contracts). A fitness function suite for a Golden Path class is maintained by the Platform Engineering team alongside the path template.
page_texts.12:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

Current development produces architecturally inconsistent services because there are no executable tests that assert architectural properties. A HIPAA-compliant REST service may log PHI to structured output, lack an audit event for a data access operation, or omit TLS enforcement — none of these are caught by file structure checks or unit tests. When AI agents generate HIPAA-scoped services, these violations occur silently and accumulate across the portfolio.
page_texts.13:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

- Fitness functions must be deterministic: same code must produce same result on every run
- Must not depend on external services in the test environment — test doubles or injectable fakes required for external dependencies
- Must produce structured results compatible with the evidence store schema
- Execution time budget: fitness function suite per service must complete in < 5 minutes
page_texts.15:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

For each Golden Path, the fitness function suite is a collection of independently executable test cases, each asserting one architectural property. The suite is structured in categories matching the Verification Contract (observability, security controls, resilience, data handling). Each test case invokes the service or inspects its build artifact, asserts the property, and produces a structured pass/fail result with detail. The suite is versioned in the Golden Path catalog repository alongside the path template. On pipeline failure, a detailed report is produced as a conformance evidence artifact and the pipeline is halted at that stage.

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#components]

### Components

| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
|---|---|---|
| Suite Runner | Orchestrates fitness function execution; starts test service instance; collects results | Golden Path Catalog (PTN-GOV-AI-001) |
| Observability Checks | Verifies health endpoint, metrics endpoint, structured logging format, trace context injection | Service build artifact |
| Security Checks | Verifies no PHI in log output, audit events emitted for data access, no secrets in environment variables | Service build artifact |
| Resilience Checks | Verifies dead-letter queue configuration, circuit breaker presence, retry configuration with backoff | Service build artifact and configuration |
| Fitness Report Writer | Serializes all results to evidence store schema; attaches as pipeline artifact | Compliance Evidence Store (PTN-GOV-AI-004) |
page_texts.18:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#interactions]

### Interactions

1. Build stage produces deployable artifact
2. Suite Runner starts a local/test-environment instance of the service with test configuration
3. Each check category invokes the service or inspects its artifact and asserts its architectural properties
4. Fitness Report Writer aggregates all results into a structured report
5. On all checks passing: suite exits 0, pipeline proceeds to Policy Gate
6. On any check failing: suite exits non-zero, pipeline halts, report is stored, exception routing begins
page_texts.19:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#variations]

### Variations

- **Static analysis variant**: Some fitness functions can be implemented as static analysis on the compiled artifact or source code rather than requiring a running service — useful for dependency checks and annotation validation
- **Graduated enforcement**: New fitness functions for a Golden Path can be introduced in warn-only mode for one release cycle before graduating to fail-hard, allowing teams time to remediate
- **Environment-scoped**: Certain fitness functions (e.g., actual audit event delivery to SIEM) run only against staging or production, not in unit CI runs

page_texts.23:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#phase-1-core-suite-per-golden-path]

#### Phase 1: Core Suite per Golden Path

1. For each Golden Path published in Phase 1 of the catalog, identify the architectural properties in the Verification Contract that require execution-time verification
2. Implement the observability fitness functions first — health endpoint, metrics exposure, structured logging format; these apply to all Golden Path classes
3. Implement security fitness functions specific to each path class (PHI log scanning for HIPAA paths, audit event verification for regulated data paths)
4. Implement resilience fitness functions (DLQ check for event-driven paths, circuit breaker detection for service-mesh-integrated paths)
5. Run the suites against the Golden Path reference implementation to baseline expected results
page_texts.24:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#phase-2-pipeline-integration-and-rollout]

#### Phase 2: Pipeline Integration and Rollout

1. Add the fitness suite stage to the enterprise standard CI/CD pipeline template, positioned after build and before policy gate
2. Integrate fitness reports with the compliance evidence store — each report links to the pipeline run, repository, declared Golden Path, and catalog version
3. Deploy to pilot teams in warn-only mode; review all failures to distinguish genuine violations from test harness issues
4. Switch to fail-hard mode after 2–4 week pilot
page_texts.25:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#phase-3-continuous-improvement]

#### Phase 3: Continuous Improvement

1. Add new fitness functions as new architectural requirements emerge or as violations are discovered in production
2. Quarterly review of fitness function suite effectiveness — remove tests that never fail (possibly duplicate coverage), add tests for properties found violated in audits

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#fitness-function-type-selection-guide]

### Fitness Function Type Selection Guide

When authoring a new check for the Verification Contract, use this guide to determine whether it belongs in a static analysis check, a fitness function, or elsewhere:

| Check Property | Recommended Approach | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| File/directory presence | Conformance Gate (Layer 1) | No execution needed; evaluable from file system metadata |
| Import or dependency presence | Conformance Gate (Layer 1) | Evaluable from `requirements.txt`, `pom.xml`, or `package.json` without running the service |
| HTTP endpoint responds correctly | Fitness Function (Layer 2) | Requires running service; endpoint may exist in code but fail to serve |
| Log output does not contain PHI | Fitness Function (Layer 2) | Requires invoking the service to observe actual log output |
| Kubernetes manifest resource limits | Policy-as-Code (Layer 3) | Evaluable from manifest file without running the service; OPA is the right evaluator |
| Terraform encryption properties | Policy-as-Code (Layer 3) | Plan file is sufficient input for OPA evaluation before provisioning |
| PHI not in production logs (at scale) | Runtime Monitor (Layer 4) | Cannot be fully verified in a build pipeline; requires observing production traffic patterns |
| Audit events emitted under normal load | Runtime Monitor (Layer 4) | Only observable in production with real traffic volume |
| Configuration drift (manual patches) | Runtime Monitor (Layer 4) | Detected by comparing live state to declared state — post-deployment |

**Key rule**: If a property can be verified without executing the service, it belongs in Layer 1 or Layer 3. If it requires executing the service but is verifiable in a short-lived test instance, it belongs in Layer 2 (fitness function). If it requires production traffic or time, it belongs in Layer 4.

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#example-1-observability-fitness-function-pythonpytest]

#### Example 1: Observability Fitness Function (Python/pytest)

```python
# fitness/observability/test_health_endpoint.py
import pytest
import httpx

BASE_URL = "http://localhost:8080"

def test_health_endpoint_present():
    """Golden Path requirement: every service must expose GET /health."""
    response = httpx.get(f"{BASE_URL}/health", timeout=5.0)
    assert response.status_code == 200, (
        f"FITNESS-OBS-001 FAIL: /health returned {response.status_code}. "
        "Every Golden Path service must expose a /health endpoint returning 200."
    )

def test_health_response_has_required_fields():
    """Health response must include status and version fields."""
    response = httpx.get(f"{BASE_URL}/health", timeout=5.0)
    body = response.json()
    assert "status" in body, "FITNESS-OBS-002 FAIL: /health response missing 'status' field"
    assert "version" in body, "FITNESS-OBS-003 FAIL: /health response missing 'version' field"
```

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#example-2-hipaa-security-fitness-function]

#### Example 2: HIPAA Security Fitness Function

```python
# fitness/security/test_phi_logging.py
import re
import httpx

# Patterns indicating PHI in log output
PHI_PATTERNS = [
    r'\b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b',          # SSN pattern
    r'\b[A-Z][a-z]+ [A-Z][a-z]+\b',    # Full name pattern (simplified)
    r'\bDOB\s*:\s*\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}',  # Date of birth label
    r'\bMRN\s*:\s*\w+',                 # Medical record number label
]

def test_no_phi_in_structured_logs(captured_log_output: str):
    """FITNESS-SEC-001: No PHI must appear in structured log output."""
    for pattern in PHI_PATTERNS:
        matches = re.findall(pattern, captured_log_output)
        assert not matches, (
            f"FITNESS-SEC-001 FAIL: Potential PHI found in log output matching pattern '{pattern}'. "
            f"Found {len(matches)} matches. PHI must never appear in log output."
        )
```

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#example-4-resilience-fitness-function--circuit-breaker-presence-check]

#### Example 4: Resilience Fitness Function — Circuit Breaker Presence Check

Verifies that outbound HTTP clients are wrapped with a circuit breaker, as required by the GP-001 resilience specification:

```python
# fitness/resilience/test_circuit_breaker.py
import ast
import os
import pytest

DEPENDENCY_INJECTION_FILES = [
    'src/infrastructure/http_client.py',
    'src/infrastructure/downstream_client.py',
]

CIRCUIT_BREAKER_DECORATORS = ['@circuit', '@CircuitBreaker', 'CircuitBreaker(']

def find_outbound_http_clients(repo_root: str) -> list[str]:
    """Returns a list of files containing httpx.AsyncClient or requests.Session instantiation."""
    clients = []
    for dirpath, _, filenames in os.walk(os.path.join(repo_root, 'src')):
        for filename in filenames:
            if not filename.endswith('.py'):
                continue
            filepath = os.path.join(dirpath, filename)
            code = open(filepath).read()
            if 'httpx.AsyncClient' in code or 'requests.Session' in code:
                clients.append(filepath)
    return clients

@pytest.mark.fitness
def test_outbound_http_clients_have_circuit_breakers(repo_root):
    """
    FITNESS-RESIL-003: All outbound HTTP clients must be wrapped with a circuit breaker.
    GP-001 Verification Contract check type: fitness-function, layer 2.
    """
    client_files = find_outbound_http_clients(repo_root)
    assert client_files, (
        'FITNESS-RESIL-003 SKIP: No outbound HTTP client files found. '
        'If this service has no downstream HTTP calls, add explicit exemption to service.yaml.'
    )

    violations = []
    for filepath in client_files:
        code = open(filepath).read()
        has_breaker = any(decorator in code for decorator in CIRCUIT_BREAKER_DECORATORS)
        if not has_breaker:
            violations.append(filepath)

    assert not violations, (
        f'FITNESS-RESIL-003 FAIL: The following files contain HTTP clients '
        f'without circuit breaker wrapping: {violations}. '
        f'Wrap all outbound HTTP clients with pybreaker CircuitBreaker or equivalent. '
        f'See GP-001 resilience specification: catalog/golden-paths/gp-001/resilience.md'
    )
```

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

- Write fitness functions that test exactly one architectural property — small, focused tests are easier to debug and maintain
- Use descriptive failure messages with the fitness function ID (e.g., FITNESS-OBS-001) so reports are actionable without reading source code
- Keep test execution deterministic: no random data, no time-dependent assertions, no external service dependencies
- Maintain fitness suites in the Golden Path catalog repository — co-locate suites with the paths they verify
- Review fitness function coverage quarterly: properties found violated in production that weren't caught by fitness functions indicate gaps that need new tests
page_texts.33:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

- **Fitness functions that test application logic**: These belong in unit tests. Fitness functions must test architectural properties exclusively — otherwise the boundary between architecture verification and application testing collapses.
- **Slow suites**: A suite taking > 5 minutes will be bypassed or pushed to nightly runs by teams under delivery pressure. Keep each check fast; parallelize the suite.
- **Testing against production endpoints**: Fitness functions must run in the CI/CD pipeline against a test instance, not against production. Production behavioral verification belongs to Layer 4 (Runtime Monitors).
- **No test for failure paths**: An observability fitness function that only tests the happy path may miss that the error path suppresses log output or emits the wrong structure.

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#real-world-example-1]

### Real-World Example 1

**Context:** An AI agent generates a HIPAA REST microservice. The generated service includes a debug logging statement that writes the full request body — containing PHI — to structured output.

**Implementation:** The HIPAA security fitness function suite runs against the built service image. The PHI log-scanning check invokes a representative API endpoint with synthetic PHI data and inspects the captured log output. The check fails with FITNESS-SEC-001.

**Outcome:** PHI logging violation caught in the pipeline before deployment. The agent context includes the fitness failure detail; on regeneration the debug statement is replaced with a sanitized log entry. No PHI ever reaches a log aggregation system.
page_texts.41:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#real-world-example-2]

### Real-World Example 2

**Context:** A developer authors an event-driven consumer service and forgets to configure the dead-letter queue for the Kafka consumer group.

**Implementation:** The resilience fitness function suite checks for DLQ configuration as required by the Event-Driven Consumer Golden Path. The check inspects the consumer configuration file for the DLQ binding and fails when it is absent.

**Outcome:** The developer is informed of the missing DLQ configuration at build time, not in a production incident when message processing fails at scale.
page_texts.42:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#real-world-example-3]

### Real-World Example 3

**Context:** Platform Engineering publishes `GP-007` (FedRAMP Moderate REST Microservice). The path requires 3 fitness functions not present in GP-001: FIPS-validated cryptography check, session timeout check, and MFA annotation check. All 3 must be authored and validated before GP-007 can be published.

**Implementation:** The Platform Engineering team authors `FedRAMP-specific.py` as an additive fitness suite that runs after the base GP-001 suite. The FIPS check inspects the service's Python environment for the `cryptography` package compiled against OpenSSL-FIPS. The session timeout check invokes the auth endpoint and measures actual session TTL by inspecting response headers. The MFA check looks for the `@requires_mfa` decorator on all endpoints in the `auth` router. All 3 functions are validated against a known-good GP-007 reference implementation before suite publication.

**Outcome:** GP-007 is published with a complete 17-function fitness suite (14 inherited from GP-001 + 3 FedRAMP additions). The suite runs in 4.2 minutes — within the 5-minute target. The first team to adopt GP-007 passes the suite on their second pipeline run (first run failed on missing `@requires_mfa` on one endpoint).

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#scenario-3-monorepo-fitness-suite-management]

#### Scenario 3: Monorepo Fitness Suite Management

The claims-processing team manages a monorepo with 3 services: a REST API (GP-001), a message consumer (GP-004), and a batch processor (GP-002). Each sub-path declares its Golden Path in `service.yaml`. The GitHub Actions workflow uses a matrix strategy to run 3 parallel fitness suites. The matrix is driven by the `service.yaml` declarations: each suite runs in its own container with the correct path's test suite image. Total pipeline time: 4.8 minutes for all 3 suites running in parallel. If only one sub-path's files change in a PR, the workflow uses path filters to run only the affected suite, bringing the feedback time to under 2 minutes for single-service changes.

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#before-problem-state]

#### Before (Problem State)

- **Verification consistency**: Architectural properties (PHI log scanning, DLQ presence, observability wiring) are verified by human reviewers whose attention and memory of the Golden Path specification varies; some reviews catch violations, others miss them
- **PHI logging risk**: A debug statement writing PHI to logs may pass 10 reviews before a security-focused reviewer catches it; by then it may have shipped to staging
- **Missing DLQ**: A Kafka consumer missing a dead-letter queue configuration passes code review because reviewers rarely check consumer configuration files in detail; the gap surfaces in a production incident
- **Architecture compliance evidence**: Claiming "this service meets the HIPAA Golden Path" relies on developer attestation; no machine-generated evidence exists

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#after-solution-state]

#### After (Solution State)

- **Verification consistency**: Fitness functions run on every commit against the declared Golden Path; the same 14 checks run for every developer, every AI agent, every pipeline — with no variability
- **PHI logging risk**: A debug statement writing PHI to logs fails `FITNESS-SEC-001` in the build pipeline within 3 minutes; the violation is caught before any human reviews the PR
- **Missing DLQ**: The resilience fitness function fails at build time with: `FITNESS-RESIL-001 FAIL: consumer group 'claims-consumer' has no DLQ binding declared in consumer-config.yaml`
- **Architecture compliance evidence**: Every pipeline run writes a structured fitness results record to the Compliance Evidence Store; architecture compliance is machine-attested on every commit

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-001-architecture-fitness-function-pattern.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

**Problem:** Architectural properties (PHI log scanning, DLQ presence, observability, audit events) cannot be verified by file structure checks alone and are verified inconsistently by human reviewers.

**Solution:** Executable tests that run in the CI/CD pipeline, invoke the service or inspect its artifact, and assert architectural properties as pipeline stage gates — distinct from unit tests and integration tests.

**When to Use:**
- Verifying execution-time architectural properties for any Golden Path class
- Any pipeline requiring Golden Path conformance beyond structural file checks

**Key Benefits:**
- Architectural properties verified on every commit, not just when reviewed manually
- Human review redirected to semantic correctness exclusively
- Pipeline gates prevent architecturally non-conforming services from reaching deployment

**Implementation Complexity:** Medium-High

**Prerequisites:** Golden Path Catalog (PTN-GOV-AI-001), Verification Contract (PTN-GOV-AI-003), Conformance Gate operational (PTN-INFRA-GOV-001)

**Related Patterns:** PTN-GOV-AI-001, PTN-GOV-AI-003, PTN-INFRA-GOV-001, PTN-INFRA-GOV-002, PTN-APP-GOV-003
